note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — NAKED COMB-TIP STINGER
tiles.details: Existing species panels 1–3 show spreading hairs and the exposed terminal branch-axis extension. That pointed RACHIS is not an awn attached to a lemma. Measure the bare part from the final attached spikelet on a mature undamaged comb; existing photos establish the silhouette, not a calibrated 5–10 mm measurement.
tiles.short: On one intact hairy grama comb, trace the bare rachis about 5–10 mm beyond the last spikelet.
tiles.status: REAL PIXEL-VISIBLE BRANCH TIP — MEASURED TIP STILL NEEDED

tiles.heading: 02 · PERENNIAL TUFT, TRUE LIGULE AND COLLAR
tiles.details: Published Iowa State treatment describes a hair-fringe ligule about 0.2–0.5 mm. Separate true inner-junction ligule hairs from the longer papillose-based hairs on basal blade margins and from branch hairs. The three archived target photographs do not demonstrate a complete rooted crown or calibrated true ligule. Do not add an anatomy arrow without a real exposed collar.
tiles.short: Tufted perennial; at the blade–sheath seam seek a very short 0.2–0.5 mm hair-fringe ligule.

tiles.heading: 03 · COUNT COMBS AND MATURE SPIKELETS
tiles.details: Published ranges, not measurements from the unscaled images. Count branches on ONE connected flowering culm, then use a millimeter ruler on a mature comb and an intact ~5–6 mm spikelet. The naked 5–10 mm rachis tip and the spikelet body are separate measurements.
tiles.short: Usually 1–4 one-sided combs, each about 1.5–3 cm with roughly 20–50 spikelets.
tiles.status: REAL TARGET COMBS — SCALE AND COMPLETE CULM MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES, TWO FLORETS AND AWN ORIGINS
tiles.details: A mature spikelet has a fertile basal floret and one or two reduced sterile florets. Dissect BOTH glumes separately. The fertile lemma may have short awns (central ~0.2–2.5 mm), while the reduced sterile lemma often has THREE awns about 2–4(–6) mm. Do not mistake the terminal naked rachis for a lemma awn or infer which floret carries a bristle from an overview image.
tiles.short: Spikelet ~5–6 mm; lower glume ~1.4–3.5 mm, upper ~3–6 mm; fertile lemma ~2–4.5 mm.
tiles.status: PUBLISHED REPRODUCTIVE ANATOMY — DISSECTED 1-MM-SCALE PHOTO MISSING

tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: Comparison panel 4 is BLUE GRAMA, not hairy grama. Bouteloua gracilis usually has 1–3 curved eyebrow combs with spikelets reaching close to their tips; hairy grama has spreading reproductive hairs and a conspicuous bare tip. B. pectinata may overlap in size and hairiness, and B. trifida has much shorter narrow appressed branches. Compare ripe spikelets and verified rachis tips, not purple color alone.
tiles.short: Blue grama usually lacks the long bare stinger; pectinata often has longer, more numerous combs.
tiles.status: REAL LOOK-ALIKE PANEL — SAME-SCALE COMPARISON NEEDED

tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE / TWO HANDOFFS
tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO (Grass Photo-Finish): one voucher-linked rooted Central Texas perennial with entire flowering culm and comb count; 1-mm-calibrated 5–10 mm naked rachis tip; true 0.2–0.5 mm hair-fringe ligule plus basal papillose hairs; intact ~5–6 mm spikelet with separately exposed glumes, fertile and sterile lemmas and distinct awn origins; matched blue grama and pectinata combs. NEEDS_SITE_QA (Public Learner Readiness): verify all three physical JPEGs, individual CC BY-SA 4.0 / CC BY-SA 2.0 / CC0 1.0 credits and conditions, six existing gross arrows against actual pixels, other-species panel labels, six tile layouts and live/mobile display. Do not mark FINISHED or claim a new photograph/arrow.
tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: three real archived species photos, but decisive measured microanatomy is missing.

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: Inspect the END of one intact comb and look for a conspicuous bare, pointed branch-axis extension ('stinger') beyond the last spikelets. On fresh branches check for long spreading hairs and on basal blades for papillose-based hairs. Hairiness alone varies and does not trump terminal spikelet/rachis anatomy.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: FIRST PHOTO: inspect the taxon-labelled Juan Carlos Fonseca Mata flowering-branch image with the existing two gross pointers to conspicuous hairs and its projecting naked rachis tip; it is NOT whole-plant habit despite its old filename.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Published Iowa State treatment describes a hair-fringe ligule about 0.2–0.5 mm. Separate true inner-junction ligule hairs from the longer papillose-based hairs on basal blade margins and from branch hairs. The three archived target photographs do not demonstrate a complete rooted crown or calibrated true ligule. Do not add an anatomy arrow without a real exposed collar.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Published ranges, not measurements from the unscaled images. Count branches on ONE connected flowering culm, then use a millimeter ruler on a mature comb and an intact ~5–6 mm spikelet. The naked 5–10 mm rachis tip and the spikelet body are separate measurements.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Compared with blue grama, hairy grama has more conspicuously hairy reproductive parts and a naked projecting rachis tip; blue comb spikelets continue toward the tip. Taller B. pectinata often has longer, straighter and more numerous combs, but their features overlap enough to require mature units and provenance. Texas grama bears several very short highly awned/fuzzy branches rather than a few longer solid combs.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: FIELD CLOSE-UP · spreading bristles and bare branch extension — archived photograph
panels.caption: Source photograph identified as Bouteloua hirsuta from Dolores Hidalgo, Mexico, NOT a Hays County voucher. The foreground comb shows many long pale spreading hairs and a narrow bare extension beyond the crowded flowering units. The visible projection is a branch-axis feature, NOT an individual lemma awn; its precise length and the microscopic glume hair bases cannot be measured here.
panels.creator: Juan Carlos Fonseca Mata
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: 1 · The naked branch-tip 'stinger'
panels.caption: The bare pointed rachis extends leftward beyond the last fertile spikelets. Thin pale hairs project from the photographed branch. Neither is a blade ligule.
panels.creator: Matt Lavin
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: 2 · Comb tip above dangling anthers
panels.caption: The long slender naked portion extends to the left of the packed flowering units. Cream-colored structures drooping underneath are anthers, not spikelet bristles.
panels.creator: Patrick Alexander
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: HAIRY GRAMA — second-glume spreading hairs and bare branch extension (real macro)
panels.caption: Original hairy grama reproduction photograph by Matt Lavin. Prominent second glumes carry long spreading hairs, described by the photographer as arising from dark sessile glands. Unlike blue grama, the flower-bearing branch ends in a longer naked extension. This is NOT the ligule or leaf collar; glume hair gland points remain to be verified in full-resolution pixels.
panels.creator: Matt Lavin
panels.modifications: RGB JPEG reencoded, EXIF/GPS removed and scaled down; full composition retained
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

memory_rule: Find an intact one-sided flowering comb; don't just notice its purple or tan color.
safety_note: Three real species-labelled CC/CC0 JPEGs are physically archived, but none shows complete rooted habit or true ligule and measured floret anatomy. Existing six gross-image arrows retained; no micro labels have been added.
